passages.title: The Evolution of Public Museums
passages.intro: An academic-style overview of history, examining evidence and practical implications.
paras: Many early collections were assembled by wealthy individuals or institutions. Access to museums expanded at different rates in different places.
Explanatory labels influence how visitors understand displayed objects. Consultation may reveal histories that collections previously neglected.
Some objects cannot remain on display continuously because light can damage them. Online catalogues help researchers and visitors find collection items.
Visitor numbers alone do not show what people learned. Many institutions now study how visitors engage with exhibits.

passages.intro: An academic-style overview of work, examining evidence and practical implications.
paras: Remote arrangements can give employees more control over when and where they work. Working apart can reduce spontaneous conversations between colleagues.
Written records help colleagues in different locations coordinate tasks. Too many online meetings can leave less time for concentrated work.
Teams across time zones need to schedule communication thoughtfully. Evaluating completed work can be more useful than monitoring online presence.
People who join remotely may need additional help building relationships. Hybrid arrangements are easier to manage when expectations are explicit.

passages.title: The Economics of Repair
passages.intro: An academic-style overview of economics, examining evidence and practical implications.
paras: Repair can keep a product in use for longer rather than replacing it. Products are harder to repair when replacement parts are unavailable.
High repair labour costs can make buying a new item seem more economical. A product's design determines how easily it can be taken apart.
Community repair events allow people to exchange practical skills. Some warranty terms discourage or restrict repairs by unauthorised providers.
The environmental advantage of repair varies with the product and process. Regulations can encourage manufacturers to provide parts and repair information.
